# dorgql

> Generates an M-by-N real orthogonal matrix Q with orthonormal columns.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dorgql from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dorgql';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dorgql( order, M, N, K, A, LDA, TAU, strideTAU, WORK ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows of Q (M >= 0)<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns of Q (0 <= N <= M)<br>Rejects `N < 0 \|\| N > M` |
| `K` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elementary reflectors (0 <= K <= N)<br>Rejects `K < 0 \|\| K > N` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Column-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, M)`<br>Row-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `TAU` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length K</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | `TAU` stride length |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, N)</sub> | **out** · Workspace of length at least `max(1,N)`; `N*NB` (`NB = 32`) enables the blocked path when `K > 128`; if `null`, a workspace of the optimal size is allocated |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix Q. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix Q. $M \ge N \ge 0$.
- `K`: The number of elementary reflectors whose product defines the matrix Q. $N \ge K \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the (n-k+i)-th column must contain the vector which defines the elementary reflector H(i), for $i = 1$,2,...,k, as returned by DGEQLF in the last k columns of its array argument A. On exit, the M-by-N matrix Q.
- `TAU`: `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i), as returned by DGEQLF.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `N < 0 \|\| N > M`)
- `RangeError` fourth argument is invalid (rejected when `K < 0 \|\| K > N`)
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, M )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dorgql.ndarray(
    M, N, K,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    TAU, strideTAU, offsetTAU,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of rows of Q (M >= 0)<br>Requires `M ≥ 0` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns of Q (0 <= N <= M)<br>Rejects `N < 0 \|\| N > M` |
| `K` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elementary reflectors (0 <= K <= N)<br>Rejects `K < 0 \|\| K > N` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix (M x N) |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A |
| `TAU` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length K</sub> | Scalar factors of reflectors (length K) |
| ↳ `strideTAU` | `integer` | Stride for TAU |
| ↳ `offsetTAU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for TAU |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, N)</sub> | **out** · Workspace of length at least `max(1,N)`; `N*NB` (`NB = 32`) enables the blocked path when `K > 128` |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix Q. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix Q. $M \ge N \ge 0$.
- `K`: The number of elementary reflectors whose product defines the matrix Q. $N \ge K \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the (n-k+i)-th column must contain the vector which defines the elementary reflector H(i), for $i = 1$,2,...,k, as returned by DGEQLF in the last k columns of its array argument A. On exit, the M-by-N matrix Q.
- `TAU`: `TAU(i)` must contain the scalar factor of the elementary reflector H(i), as returned by DGEQLF.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` second argument is invalid (rejected when `N < 0 \|\| N > M`)
- `RangeError` third argument is invalid (rejected when `K < 0 \|\| K > N`)

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N <= 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument has an illegal value

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dorgql from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dorgql';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const A = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const TAU = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const WORK = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dorgql( 'row-major', N, N, N, A, N, TAU, 1, WORK );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = dorgql.ndarray( N, N, N, A, N, 1, 0, TAU, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DORGQL`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DORGQL generates an M-by-N real matrix Q with orthonormal columns, which is defined as the last N columns of a product of K elementary reflectors of order M

$$
Q = H(k) \cdots H(2) H(1)
$$

as returned by DGEQLF.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
